budget.derivation: eps_struct = min(B_evid, eps/3) = min(5.4210e-20, 3.3333e-10) = 5.4210e-20; eps_rate = eps_chan = (eps - eps_struct)/2 = 5.0000e-10; sum = eps = 1.0000e-09. The structural family's proven bound is B_evid(n) whatever its share, so a larger share buys it nothing (C-2); the cap at eps/3 keeps the split from ever being worse than the even one.

attributions.rationale: the honest run is the run every null in this package describes, so every threshold fires on it with at most its own proven bound; this is the one row that may be excluded on a mismatch or a channel signal, because for the null itself those are the departure the threshold was built to bound rather than the channel's noise level. excluded by ['rate:mismatch_rate:Bob', 'rate:mismatch_rate:Charlie'], whose nulls this position leaves intact; the exclusion is mistaken with probability at most 0.0000e+00.

a declaration drawn independently of the recipients' records leaves the matched count's law exactly Binomial(n, 1/|B|) and touches no wire integer, no forwarding hop and no ledger; only the eigenvalues at positions that do match are disturbed, and each of those survives with probability 1/2 (sih141.protocol.analysis.FORGER_MATCHED_MISMATCH_PROBABILITY), so the mismatch count is zero with probability 2**-|M_R| and the signal is required rather than merely predicted. supported by ['rate:mismatch_rate:Bob', 'rate:mismatch_rate:Charlie']; an honest run trips all of that evidence with probability at most 0.0000e+00, which is a bound against the honest null and not a bound on having named the wrong adversary (C-6).

Mallory runs the protocol correctly with a key pair of her own, so every statistic on the transcript is drawn from the honest law; assumption (AUTH) puts this position out of model rather than pretending a detector reaches it. never named and never ruled out: assumption (AUTH) puts this position out of model, and a hypothesis silently missing from a table reads as one that was excluded.

he forwards a declaration built from his own raw log, which after Phase A' is roughly half of what the receiving verifier holds, so that verifier's matched count moves from n/3 to 2n/3 -- sqrt(n/2) standard deviations of the null, 9.80 at n = 192 and 240 at DEFAULT_PARAMS, with the derived upper-tail threshold strictly between the two means, which is what makes COUNT_HIGH a requirement and not a hope; his forwarded declaration is not Alice's, so the pair's counts name two declarations; he presents it into a fresh round, so no ledger entry is spent twice. not supported: this position produces ['count-high'] with probability essentially one, and on this run that was evaluated and did not fire. Withheld rather than refuted -- a signal that did not fire carries no bound, only a false-negative statement nothing here derives.

he understates one integer on the Phase C' wire and nothing else: his own scored matched count is untouched, so the two part company, and the lie is downward by construction -- an upper tail, a second declaration on the forwarding hop and a spent round are all three out of a count-exchange seam's reach. nothing fired that this position predicts, and nothing that excludes it -- an absence of evidence, which is not evidence of absence and is not reported as one.

he re-presents a captured declaration, which the consumed-records ledger and the session binding both record, and which is not the declaration Alice sent this run; that declaration was drawn independently of the receiving verifier's current record, so every count null is left exactly where it was while the eigenvalues at matched positions disagree. LEDGER is predicted and NOT required: the ledger check is sound in one direction only -- a replay that burns its round through a rejection leaves the refusal count at zero (finding 4 of the structural family). supported by ['rate:mismatch_rate:Bob', 'rate:mismatch_rate:Charlie']; an honest run trips all of that evidence with probability at most 0.0000e+00, which is a bound against the honest null and not a bound on having named the wrong adversary (C-6).

the matched set is decided by basis agreement, and a trace-preserving map on the entanglement resource acts on the teleported eigenstate; it cannot move a basis, so it cannot move a count, a floor, a declaration or a bookkeeping equality. CHANNEL is predicted and NOT required: a weak enough deviation clears a short check sample, and this layer bounds false positives and never false negatives. supported by ['rate:mismatch_rate:Bob', 'rate:mismatch_rate:Charlie']; an honest run trips all of that evidence with probability at most 0.0000e+00, which is a bound against the honest null and not a bound on having named the wrong adversary (C-6).

nulls.note: detect() takes TWO nulls and both default to a perfect link: channel_error_rate for the rate family and tolerated_depolarising for the channel family. They are two parameterisations of the same physics and neither is converted into the other, because that would state a null the operator did not ask for. Stating only one leaves an honest run over a noisy link DETECTED with an adversary named -- 12/12 at L = 192, strength 0.03125, over twelve seeds, against 0/12 with both stated. Neither is ever inferred from the transcript: at check_fraction = 0 the transcript carries no estimate of either, and guessing would be inventing a null.

ground_truth.label: Impersonation, one seam
ground_truth.notes: Mallory held Alice's signing seam only, so her declaration and the recipients' records were produced by different parties. The transcript cannot separate this from an outside forgery, and the detector names the group.
ground_truth.model_note: Seizing one of Alice's two seams is inside the threat model. The transcript cannot separate this from an outside forgery, and the detector says so rather than picking one. The adversary owns its randomness and never reads the session's (D6), so its choices are reproducible from the request seed and independent of the run.
ground_truth.note: Everything under this key is the ADVERSARY's own log and the harness's. detect() reads a JSON transcript and nothing else, so none of it reached the verdict beside it.

link.description: an ideal Phi+ resource on both links
link.note: The link's true error rate is the ADVERSARY's ground truth and the detector never reads it. detect() is told two nulls, both defaulting to a perfect link: channel_error_rate for the rate family and tolerated_depolarising for the channel family. When either disagrees with the link, an HONEST run departs from a law it was scored against and fires correctly -- that is the null being wrong about the link, not an attack, and both verifiers still accept.
